However, before he entered the city, he ordered it to be announced to those gathered that he would never recognize them as judges. Afterward, when asked by the Council whether that Instruction was his, he indeed denied it was composed by him; nevertheless, he openly professed that he entirely adopted, held, and approved of it as his own, until he should be convinced of the errors the bishops had condemned in it. In truth, the obstinacy of this man could not be overcome. Therefore, by the sentence of the Council, he was interdicted from every function, both episcopal and priestly, and a Vicar General was appointed for his diocese. It would take too long to recount the outcries and tumults this scene produced. Twelve bishops protested against this sentence and delivered a protest to the King himself. Reliqua interrogatoria, quæ hïc defunt, Visitatores pro sua discretione suppleant.

Denique omnes & singulos Decanos Rurales nostræ Constantiensis Diœcesis, seriò admonitos volumus, ut præter hanc annuam visitationem, ipsi nihilominùs omni tempore diligenter superintendant, solicitéque invigilent, an ea, quæ in Concilio Tridentino, Statutísque Synodalibus decreta & definita sunt, rectè executioni mandentur. Itáque ne ex parte quoque nostra aliquid desideretur, curabunt Decani, ut toties quoties Capitula Ruralia in posterum convocaturi & celebraturi sunt, id Vicario vel Fiscali nostro, ad minùs mensem antè, per litteras significent, quò nostros, si opus fuerit, ad ea ablegare, & an huic mandato per omnia reverenter pareatis & obediatis, indagare valeamus. Deus Opt. Maximus conatus nostros & vestros benè fortunet, ad laudem & gloriam nominis sui, ad utilitatem quoque nostram, totiúsque Ecclesiæ suæ sanctæ, A M E N.

The remaining interrogatories that are lacking here, let the Visitors supplement according to their discretion.

Finally, we wish all and singular Rural Deans of our Diocese of Constance to be seriously admonished that, besides this annual visitation, they shall nevertheless diligently superintend and solicitously watch at all times whether those things which were decreed and defined in the Council of Trent and the Synodal Statutes are correctly mandated for execution. Therefore, so that nothing may be lacking on our part, the Deans shall ensure that as often as they are to convene and celebrate Rural Chapters in the future, they shall signify this to our Vicar or Fiscal by letter at least a month beforehand, so that we may be able to send our own representatives if need be, and investigate whether you reverently obey and comply with this mandate in all things. May God the Most High and Good make our efforts and yours prosper, for the praise and glory of His name, and also for our benefit and that of His whole holy Church, AMEN.
